- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

134		if update.UID != nil && !base.UIDMatcher.MatchString(*update.UID) {
135			return errors.New("invalid uid")
136		}
137		return s.driver.UpdateMemo(ctx, update)
138	}

141		// Clean up memo_relation records where this memo is either the source or target.
142		if err := s.driver.DeleteMemoRelation(ctx, &DeleteMemoRelation{MemoID: &delete.ID}); err != nil {
143			return err
144		}
145		if err := s.driver.DeleteMemoRelation(ctx, &DeleteMemoRelation{RelatedMemoID: &delete.ID}); err != nil {
146			return err
147		}
148		// Clean up attachments linked to this memo.
149		attachments, err := s.ListAttachments(ctx, &FindAttachment{MemoID: &delete.ID})
150		if err != nil {
151			return err
152		}
153		for _, attachment := range attachments {
154			if err := s.DeleteAttachment(ctx, &DeleteAttachment{ID: attachment.ID}); err != nil {
155				return err
156			}
157		}
158		return s.driver.DeleteMemo(ctx, delete)

---

## Data Layer Overview

This is **Memos** (github.com/usememos/memos), a Go application using a classic store/driver pattern. The data layer lives in the `/bench/repo/store/` directory. It defines Go struct types for each persistent entity at the store package root, and each entity has corresponding database driver implementations for SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL under `/bench/repo/store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/`. Protobuf definitions for some payload types live under `/bench/repo/proto/store/`.

The database schema (all three dialects are equivalent) creates **11 tables**. Each table maps to a Go struct defined in the store package. Below is the complete list.

---

## Complete List of Persistent Entity Types

### 1. User
- **File:** `/bench/repo/store/user.go` (lines 29-45)
- **Table:** `user`
- **Go struct:** `User`
- **Fields:** ID, RowStatus, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs, Username, Role, Email, Nickname, PasswordHash, AvatarURL, Description
- **Related types:** `UpdateUser`, `FindUser`, `DeleteUser`, `Role` (enum: ADMIN, USER)

### 2. Memo
- **File:** `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` (lines 35-55)
- **Table:** `memo`
- **Go struct:** `Memo`
- **Fields:** ID, UID, RowStatus, CreatorID, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs, Content, Visibility, Pinned, Payload (protobuf `MemoPayload`), ParentUID (composed)
- **Related types:** `UpdateMemo`, `FindMemo`, `FindMemoPayload`, `DeleteMemo`, `Visibility` (enum: PUBLIC, PROTECTED, PRIVATE)

### 3. Attachment
- **File:** `/bench/repo/store/attachment.go` (lines 16-41)
- **Table:** `attachment`
- **Go struct:** `Attachment`
- **Fields:** ID, UID, CreatorID, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs, Filename, Blob, Type, Size, StorageType (protobuf enum), Reference, Payload (protobuf `AttachmentPayload`), MemoID, MemoUID (composed)
- **Related types:** `FindAttachment`, `UpdateAttachment`, `DeleteAttachment`

### 4. MemoRelation
- **File:** `/bench/repo/store/memo_relation.go` (lines 16-20)
- **Table:** `memo_relation`
- **Go struct:** `MemoRelation`
- **Fields:** MemoID, RelatedMemoID, Type
- **Related types:** `FindMemoRelation`, `DeleteMemoRelation`, `MemoRelationType` (enum: REFERENCE, COMMENT)

### 5. MemoShare
- **File:** `/bench/repo/store/memo_share.go` (lines 6-13)
- **Table:** `memo_share`
- **Go struct:** `MemoShare`
- **Fields:** ID, UID, MemoID, CreatorID, CreatedTs, ExpiresTs
- **Related types:** `FindMemoShare`, `DeleteMemoShare`

### 6. UserSetting
- **File:** `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go` (lines 13-17)
- **Table:** `user_setting`
- **Go struct:** `UserSetting`
- **Fields:** UserID, Key (protobuf `UserSetting_Key` enum), Value (JSON-serialized protobuf)
- **Related types:** `FindUserSetting`, `DeleteUserSetting`, `RefreshTokenQueryResult`, `PATQueryResult`

### 7. UserIdentity
- **File:** `/bench/repo/store/user_identity.go` (lines 8-15)
- **Table:** `user_identity`
- **Go struct:** `UserIdentity`
- **Fields:** ID, UserID, Provider, ExternUID, CreatedTs, UpdatedTs
- **Related types:** `FindUserIdentity`, `DeleteUserIdentity`

### 8. IdentityProvider (IDP)
- **File:** `/bench/repo/store/idp.go` (lines 12-19)
- **Table:** `idp`
- **Go struct:** `IdentityProvider`
- **Fields:** ID, UID, Name, Type (protobuf `IdentityProvider_Type`), IdentifierFilter, Config (JSON string)
- **Related types:** `FindIdentityProvider`, `UpdateIdentityProvider`, `UpdateIdentityProviderV1`, `DeleteIdentityProvider`

### 9. Inbox
- **File:** `/bench/repo/store/inbox.go` (lines 24-31)
- **Table:** `inbox`
- **Go struct:** `Inbox`
- **Fields:** ID, CreatedTs, SenderID, ReceiverID, Status, Message (protobuf `InboxMessage`)
- **Related types:** `UpdateInbox`, `FindInbox`, `DeleteInbox`, `InboxStatus` (enum: UNREAD, ARCHIVED)

### 10. Reaction
- **File:** `/bench/repo/store/reaction.go` (lines 7-14)
- **Table:** `reaction`
- **Go struct:** `Reaction`
- **Fields:** ID, CreatedTs, CreatorID, ContentID, ReactionType
- **Related types:** `FindReaction`, `DeleteReaction`

### 11. InstanceSetting (SystemSetting)

- **Table:** `system_setting`
- **Go struct:** `InstanceSetting`
- **Fields:** Name, Value (JSON-serialized protobuf), Description
- **Related types:** `FindInstanceSetting`, `DeleteInstanceSetting`

---

## Supporting Definitions

- **RowStatus** (shared enum): `/bench/repo/store/common.go` -- values NORMAL, ARCHIVED
- **Driver interface** (lists all entity CRUD methods): `/bench/repo/store/driver.go`
- **Store struct** (orchestration layer with caching): `/bench/repo/store/store.go`
- **AuthenticationConfigState / AuthenticationConfigMutation** (transactional helpers, not a separate table): `/bench/repo/store/auth_config.go`
- **DeleteUserResult** (aggregate result, not a table): `/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go`
- **DeploymentConfiguration** (in-memory runtime config, not a table): `/bench/repo/store/deployment_config.go`

## Database Schema Files

All three supported databases define the same 11 tables:
- SQLite: `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql`
- MySQL: `/bench/repo/store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql`
- PostgreSQL: `/bench/repo/store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql`

## Protobuf Payload Types (nested within entity fields)

These protobuf definitions provide structured payloads stored as JSON inside certain entity columns:
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto` -- `MemoPayload`
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/attachment.proto` -- `AttachmentPayload`, `AttachmentStorageType`
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/user_setting.proto` -- `UserSetting` (key enum and value oneof)
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/instance_setting.proto` -- `InstanceSetting`, various sub-settings
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/idp.proto` -- `IdentityProvider`, `IdentityProviderConfig`, `OAuth2Config`
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/inbox.proto` -- `InboxMessage`
